title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering and regional failover behavior
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: During a recent incident (SUP-4321) the SLO enforcer backoff logic and regional failover ordering produced thrashing between regions under bursty traffic. This caused repeated failovers and unnecessary load-shedding despite healthy capacity in a secondary region. This hotfix tightens ordering guarantees, makes backoff deterministic under concurrent enforcer evaluations, and adds a short-term guard to avoid immediate re-failovers after a regional promotion. Changes here are narrowly scoped to the enforcer and routing decision path and are intended as a fast, safe rollback/stabilization for the incident window. Summary of changes: 1) Ensure deterministic ordering when multiple region-state transitions are evaluated concurrently by introducing an ordered evaluation queue and explicit compare-and-swap on region state. 2) Add a short cooldown (configurable, default 30s) after a promotion before allowing failback/failover to another region. 3) Make backoff counters explicit per-region and persist them to the enforcer MAU to avoid loss during transient restarts. 4) Add unit + integration tests covering concurrent promotions and the cooldown path. Checklist: - [x] Reproduced issue locally with chaos test harness - [x] Implemented ordered evaluation queue + CAS to avoid race windows - [x] Added cooldown guard with config flag slo.enforcer.promotion_cooldown_seconds - [x] Added deterministic backoff counter persistence - [x] New unit and integration tests - [x] CI green, staging run validated - [x] Rollout plan: gradual canary then full rollout If this change requires additional tuning we will follow-up with SRE runbook updates (SRE-220).

review_comments: Liam Chen: Observed race in the previous implementation where two promotions could interleave and cause immediate failback. The ordered queue approach LGTM; please ensure the queue is bounded and has metrics for queue depth.
Aisha Khan: Added queue depth metric (slo_enforcer_eval_queue_depth) and bounded the queue with backpressure + metric annotation. Defaults chosen to avoid runtime regressions; made it configurable.
Sofia Patel: Can the cooldown cause increased latency for legitimate failovers? Suggest a short default (30s) and make it tunable per-customer.
Aisha Khan: Agreed; implemented promotion_cooldown_seconds with default 30s and override via env/config per-deployment. Updated docs in the SRE runbook link (SRE-220).
Evan Brooks: Tests look good; added a small integration run in staging (us-east-1 canary) and validated that thrash stopped under the reproduced load pattern. Approving for merge once CI is green.
Liam Chen: Approved after staging validation. Small nit: rename variable 'promoCooldown' to 'promotionCooldownSeconds' for consistency. Fixed in squash commit.
release_notes: Hotfix: Stabilize SLO enforcer regional promotion/failover ordering and backoff persistence. Adds promotion cooldown (default 30s) and ordered evaluation queue to prevent regional thrashing under burst load.
testing_summary: Reproduced incident locally with chaos harness and fixed; added unit tests for ordering, integration tests for concurrent promotions and cooldown behavior. Staging canary (us-east-1) ran for 2 hours under synthetic burst load with no observed thrash. CI passed: unit/integration/lint/compile.
rollout_plan: Canary rollout to 10% of region traffic (us-east-1) for 1 hour; monitor slo_enforcer_failover_rate, slo_enforcer_eval_queue_depth, error budget burn. If stable, increase to 50% for 2 hours then full rollout. Emergency rollback: revert release or toggle slo.enforcer.promotion_cooldown_seconds=0 and restart enforcer pods.
notes: This is a narrowly-scoped hotfix. Follow-up work tracked in ENG-3456 to enhance long-term stability and telemetry. No breaking API changes.
